label: input token l late in the original phase (position >= 4)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the input token is the letter l during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase; 99.4% of activation mass is on in_tok == l. Never fires at t=0-2, weakly at t=3 (rate 0.8%, low magnitude), and strongly from position 4 onward, with the highest activations (top examples) on l at positions 5-8, often the last or second-to-last original token. Magnitude grows with position/sequence length (L=9 carries 37% of mass). Does not fire at the delimiter or anywhere in the copy phase, even when l is fed back or output. Off-target activations on other tokens are rare and tiny. Remaining false positives are l tokens at positions 4+ that stay below threshold.

issues: The 't=3 rate 0.8%' figure is the rate over all tokens at t=3. Among l tokens at t=3 the rate is about 25% (dev precision 0.25 on 16.2k steps), so the wording is misleading. The underlying point, weak and low-magnitude firing at t=3, still holds (3.4% of mass).

The false positives cluster at t=4: l at t=4 has dev precision 0.72, versus 0.97 for l at t>=5. This looks like a graded ramp in position, not a separate class. Splitting by L, n_digits, vowel prev_tok, to_go or in_first did not make t=4 much sharper (precision 0.70-0.83).

Verified: zero activations at the delimiter and in the copy phase, zero at t=0-2, and 99.4% of mass on in_tok==l. The step right after an l almost never fires (prev_tok==l & in_tok!=l: precision 0.0016).

'Magnitude grows with sequence length' is mostly a side effect of position: longer sequences have more late positions. The rate by orig_idx levels off at about 3.2-3.7% for positions 5-8, and the mass share peaks at positions 5-6.
An alternative, l & (t>=4 | (t==3 & l already seen)), gives test F1 0.878, which is no better than the original 0.879.
